name: Zoth ZeUSD router opened unslippaged USDC deposits
summary: Fifty-one minutes before the exploit, a ZeUSD_Router upgrade removed whitelistedOnly from mintWithStable. The router mints ZeUSD equal to the deposited USDC amount, while WMSubVault swaps that USDC into wM on Uniswap V3 with amountOutMinimum 0, and on redemption swaps wM back with the same zero bound. With a flash loan, the attacker bought the wM/USDC 0.01% pool's wM, added its own liquidity at an extreme price, and deposited 330,979 USDC for 7,669 wM, receiving 327,619 ZeUSD. It then burned that ZeUSD after resetting the pool, so the vault sold 330,979 of its pre-existing wM to repay the attacker in USDC.
notes: The UUPS upgrade to ZeUSD_Router 0xe2574952 dropped whitelistedOnly from mintWithStable. The previous implementation 0x1e53b208 reverted the same deposit with NotWhitelisted(attacker), so this change let anyone mint ZeUSD at face value against the zero-bound subvault swap.
The last pre-exploit upgrade selected WMSubVaultUpgradeable 0x41d9db45, whose handleDeposit and handleWithdraw swap with amountOutMinimum 0.

Exact net wM depletion of WMSubVault proxy 0x3854702034855287be0fb4a040580cb89621290b in source-1. The vault also kept a 3,294.916450 USDC residual from its redemption swap, so its net value loss is about 320,008.68 USD. The attacker kept 286,902.019393 USDC. wM (wrapped M, a T-bill-backed USD stablecoin) is valued at par; DefiLlama has no historical quote. The attacker also minted 39,593,862 ZeUSD from a second 40,000,000 USDC deposit that bought 6.40 wM. It burned all of it in 0xe2644468d47e and 0x5266da8b96a0 (blocks 21959608/21959612) without redeeming, so no loss is counted for it.

Not the knot: the zero-bound swap was reachable only by whitelisted depositors until target-1's later router upgrade opened mintWithStable to the public, so the exploitable combination dates from target-1.
